subject: ChainForge x Redwood: connector & prompt-tracking integration plan
messages:
From: Evan Cho <evan@chainforge.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Ibrahim <sara@chainforge.ai>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: ChainForge x Redwood — connector proposal for prompt-tracking and SDK hooks

Hi Camila,

Thanks for the quick intro last week through Priya. ChainForge builds tooling for prompt experiment tracking, embeddings management, and live trace visualizations for multi-model chains. We think a light-weight connector into Redwood that hooks into your SDK and tracing pipeline could be mutually valuable — gives our customers turnkey observability and gives Redwood access to a broader ISV ecosystem.

High level proposal:
- A small Python adapter that plugs into LangChain/LlamaIndex-style chains and emits the common trace envelope to Redwood-compatible endpoints.
- Optional LangChain Agent middleware to auto-capture tool calls and prompt metadata (prompt templates, eval ids).
- A tracing sample format that can be consumed by both Redwood Optimize and ChainForge dashboards.

I've attached a short tech spec (chainforge-integration-spec-v1.pdf) and included a 30-minute discovery agenda link here: https://drive.google.com/chainforge-techspec

Are you available for a quick call this week to align on goals, telemetry shape, and a light SOW? We can commit to a 4-week engineering prototype if this looks promising.

Cheers,
Evan
Evan Cho
Head of Integrations, ChainForge
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Evan Cho <evan@chainforge.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 11:03:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ChainForge x Redwood — connector proposal for prompt-tracking and SDK hooks

Thanks Evan — appreciate the spec. This looks like a good fit for our ISV integrations program.

Quick notes from product:
- Primary goals: capture prompt inputs/outputs + embedding vectors metadata (model, quantization tag, seq len) and expose them as structured traces in Redwood Console/Optimize.
- We prefer adapters that are dependency-light and support both LangChain and LlamaIndex call patterns.
- Security: telemetry must be non-sensitive by default; we require an opt-in field mapping for any customer PII.

I've looped in Rachel (partnerships) and Jonas (platform engineer) to scope feasibility. Can we do Wed 5/6 at 10am PT for a 30-min sync? If that works, we'll bring an outline for acceptance criteria and a draft SOW.

Best,
Camila Reyes
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
From: Evan Cho <evan@chainforge.ai>
To: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Ibrahim <sara@chainforge.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
Date: Mon, 4 May 2026 12:05:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ChainForge x Redwood — connector proposal for prompt-tracking and SDK hooks

Wed 5/6 10am PT works for us. Draft agenda:
1) Alignment on telemetry envelope + sample events (prompt.start, prompt.complete, tool.call, embedding.generate)
2) SDK adapter surface and language support (python first; lightweight TS shim later)
3) Security & opt-in mapping for PII + sampling policy
4) Timeline / SOW / next steps

Attaching the spec again and a short sandbox snippet for our LangChain middleware. We can iterate live in the call.

Looking forward,
Evan
From: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>
To: Evan Cho <evan@chainforge.ai>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 10:35:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ChainForge x Redwood — connector proposal for prompt-tracking and SDK hooks

Thanks for the agenda and spec. A couple of engineering clarifications ahead of the call so we can be efficient:

- Trace format: are you planning to use OpenTelemetry spans as the carrier or a small JSON envelope over HTTP? We can accept either, but OTEL would make routing into our existing tracing pipelines easier.
- Sampling: for production customers we prefer a sampling flag plus deterministic sampling keys so customers can reproduce traces across services. Does ChainForge plan to include a sample_rate and sample_key?
- Auth: we will expose a short-lived ingestion token for the connector. Do you need mutual TLS or token-only? Many enterprise customers require mTLS.

Example of the envelope we'd expect (informal):
On prompt.complete: {timestamp, prompt_id, prompt_text_hash, model: {name, version, quant}, tokens_in, tokens_out, embeddings_meta}

If you can confirm OTEL vs JSON and auth preferences we can sketch integration tasks and estimate a 3-week engineering spike + 1 week polish for the prototype.

-Jonas
Senior Platform Engineer, Redwood Inference
From: Evan Cho <evan@chainforge.ai>
To: Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
Cc: Sara Ibrahim <sara@chainforge.ai>, Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>
Date: Wed, 6 May 2026 11:10:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ChainForge x Redwood — connector proposal for prompt-tracking and SDK hooks

Great questions Jonas — short answers:
- We support both: default is a tiny JSON-over-HTTPS envelope for simplicity, but we can emit OTEL spans (in proto) as an opt-in for enterprise integrations.
- Sampling: yes — our client will include sample_rate and sample_key. We also offer deterministic hashing by request id for consistent sampling.
- Auth: token-based auth by default; mTLS available for customers with strict requirements.

Given that, a 3w spike + 1w polish sounds reasonable. We'll plan to provide an initial adapter, unit tests against LangChain and LlamaIndex patterns, and a small demo app that pushes to our ChainForge dashboard.

We'll bring a proposed SOW and NDA to the call; I see Camila already attached Redwood's SOW template in the shared drive link.

Cheers,
Evan
From: Camila Reyes <camila@redwood.com>
To: Evan Cho <evan@chainforge.ai>
Cc: Rachel Kim <rachel@redwood.com>, Jonas Weber <jonas@redwood.com>, Priya Singh <priya@promptpilot.io>
Date: Thu, 7 May 2026 15:30:00 -0700
Subject: Re: ChainForge x Redwood — connector proposal for prompt-tracking and SDK hooks

Great sync today — thanks everyone for the prep. Agreed next steps and owners: 
- ChainForge: finalize adapter README + initial Python package (Evan / Sara) — target deliverable: pip-installable wheel and GitHub repo link (ETA: 3 weeks).
- Redwood Eng (Jonas): provide quick-start ingestion token and a small test harness that validates sample events against our console (ETA: 1 week).
- Partnerships (Rachel): draft the SOW and finalize commercial terms; I'll lead contract review (ETA: 2 weeks).
- Legal/Security: sign the NDA (attached) and confirm PII opt-in mapping before any customer data flows.

Attachments: NDA (nda-chainforge-redwood-signed.pdf), Redwood SOW template (redwood-sow-template.docx).

Please reply with any objections; otherwise we'll track this as CHN-4721 in HubSpot and kick off the engineering spike next Monday.

Thanks,
Camila
Head of Partnerships, Redwood Inference
